title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: which certificate's money is meant and how much of it the account still holds
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account that receives payouts from the owner's certificates of deposit, when the owner asks to move out of the account the money that the certificate which most recently paid into it put there. It defines which certificate is meant and how much of its money the account still holds.

## Policy clause

1. **Which certificate.** The certificate is the counterparty of the most recent deposit on this savings account posted as an internal transfer. It is taken only when that counterparty is a certificate of deposit of the same customer whose payout account, on the certificate record, is this savings account.
2. **No certificate identified.** When the most recent internal-transfer deposit came from any other account, no certificate money is identified and nothing is moved under this rule.
3. **Same-day deposits from different accounts.** When internal-transfer deposits from different accounts posted on that most recent date, the records do not show which of them is the most recent, and nothing is moved under this rule.
4. **Money in.** Add up every deposit on this savings account whose counterparty is that certificate. These cover the certificate's interest payouts and its maturity or grace payout, all posted as internal transfers from the certificate.
5. **Money sent back.** From that total, subtract every withdrawal already sent from this savings account to that same certificate.
6. **Floor at zero.** A difference below zero is taken as zero. The figure obtained is the net certificate money still held in the account.
7. **What is not certificate money.** Deposits from any other source, and interest the savings account itself earned, are not certificate money.

## Basis of decision

- **Authority.** The most recent internal-transfer deposit and its counterparty are read from the savings account's transaction record; whether that counterparty is a certificate of the same customer, and which account the certificate pays out to, is read from the certificate record, not from the customer's recollection.
- **Object correlation.** Only entries whose counterparty is the certificate so identified are counted, in both directions.

## Identifying the certificate (input, judgement, output)

| Most recent internal-transfer deposit came from | Certificate identified? |
|---|---|
| a certificate of the same customer whose payout account is this savings account | yes, that certificate |
| a certificate of the same customer that pays out to another account | no; nothing is moved under this rule |
| the customer's checking account or any other account | no; nothing is moved under this rule |
| two or more accounts on the same most recent date | no; the records do not show which is the most recent, so nothing is moved under this rule |

## Counting its money

| Savings account entry | Counterparty | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| certificate interest payout (internal transfer in) | the identified certificate | added |
| certificate maturity or grace payout (internal transfer in) | the identified certificate | added |
| withdrawal sent to the certificate | the identified certificate | subtracted |
| payroll ACH credit, cash, check, transfer from checking | any other source | ignored |
| savings interest credit | none; earned by the savings account | ignored |

## Worked cases (hypothetical figures)

- **Ordinary case.** The most recent internal-transfer deposit is a maturity payout from a certificate of the same customer that pays out to this account. That certificate paid interest of USD 45.10 and USD 44.90 and the maturity payout of USD 10250.00, a total of USD 10340.00. Earlier, USD 300.00 was sent from the savings account back to that certificate. Net certificate money is USD 10340.00 less USD 300.00, which is USD 10040.00. A USD 1200.00 payroll credit and USD 6.15 of savings interest are ignored.
- **Floor case.** The identified certificate paid in USD 500.00, and USD 700.00 was later sent back to it. USD 500.00 less USD 700.00 is below zero, so net certificate money is taken as USD 0.00.
- **Latest internal deposit not from a certificate.** After the certificate's last payout, the owner moved USD 200.00 in from their checking account by internal transfer. The most recent internal-transfer deposit came from a checking account, so no certificate money is identified under this rule.
- **Two sources on the same day.** On the most recent date with an internal-transfer deposit, one deposit came from the certificate and another from the owner's checking account. The records do not show which came last, so nothing is moved under this rule.

## Points of judgement

**An older certificate once paid into this account, but a different certificate paid in most recently. Which one is meant?** The one that is the counterparty of the most recent internal-transfer deposit, provided it pays out to this account.

**Is the interest the savings account earned on the certificate money part of the certificate money?** No; interest the savings account itself earned is not certificate money.
